content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "invalid_inference", "fatal": "yes", "explanation": "In Claim 3.2 the text takes an arbitrary minimal transversal T of C and immediately writes \u03c0(T)=\u220f_{p\u2208T}p, which is defined only for finite T; nothing in the text shows minimal transversals of C are finite (finiteness of members of C does not give it, as the objector's family {{x,t_n}} illustrates: an intersecting antichain of finite sets with an infinite minimal transversal). So Claim 3.2 is proved only for finite minimal transversals. This matters: in Step 4 hypothesis (iii) is invoked twice \u2014 in Case A on T\u2286I\u222aZ_s (finite, harmless), but in the closing paragraph on a minimal transversal T\u2286I\u222aZ_\u03c9, an infinite set, where finiteness of T is deduced only from T\u2208C. Hence the final contradiction rests on (iii) for a possibly infinite T, which Step 3 has not established. The gap is not repaired elsewhere."}
